items.title: Section: The Fifth and Final Aspect — Four Kinds of Antidote, Beginning with the Thirteen Requisites

items.zh: 云何建立煩惱雜染對治差別？謂略四種。一、相續成熟對治，二、近斷對治，三、一分斷對治，四、具分斷對治。如聲聞地已具說，十三種資糧道，名相續成熟對治。
items.en: How is the antidote distinction of affliction defilement established? In brief, there are four kinds. First, the continuity-maturation antidote. Second, the near-severing antidote. Third, the partial-severing antidote. Fourth, the complete-severing antidote. As already fully explained in the Stage of the Hearers, the thirteen requisites of the path of accumulation are called the continuity-maturation antidote.

items.title: Section: Kindling Fire — The Four Antidotes Now Named in Full

items.zh: 如聲聞地已具說，煗、頂、忍、世第一法，決擇分善根，名近斷對治。見道，名一分斷對治。修道，名具分斷對治。
items.en: As already fully explained in the Stage of the Hearers, the roots of goodness belonging to heat, summit, forbearance, and supreme worldly dharma are called the near-severing antidote. The path of seeing is called the partial-severing antidote. The path of cultivation is called the complete-severing antidote.

items.zh: 問：昇見道聖者，智行有何相？由幾心故，見道究竟？云何當捨見所斷惑，頓耶？漸耶？答：昇見道者所有智行，遠離眾相。爾時聖智雖緣於苦，然於苦事不起分別，謂此為苦取相而轉。如於苦諦，於集、滅、道亦復如是。爾時即於先世俗智所觀諦中，一切想相皆得解脫。絕戲論智，但於其義緣真如理離相而轉，其於爾時智行如是。

items.title: Section: Nine Minds or One — Two Ways of Speaking About the Same Breakthrough

items.zh: 建立見道由二道理。一、廣布聖教道理，有戲論建立。二、內證勝義道理，離戲論建立。依初建立增上力故，說法智品有四種心，種類智品亦有四心。隨爾所時，八種心轉；即爾所時，總說名一無間所入純奢摩他所顯之心。如是總說有九種心，見道究竟。隨爾所時，如所施設苦諦之相了別究竟；即爾所時，說名一心。第二建立增上力故，說有一心。謂唯依一證真如智相應心類，見道究竟。此中亦有奢摩他道，如前應知。
items.en: The path of seeing is established through two rationales. First, the rationale of broadly propagating the noble teaching, which involves conceptual elaboration. Second, the rationale of inwardly realising ultimate truth, which is free of conceptual elaboration. By the power of the first, dharma-wisdom is said to have four minds, and class-wisdom likewise has four minds. Throughout that time, eight minds turn; throughout that same time, this is together called the one uninterruptedly entered mind manifested by pure calm-abiding. Thus, in total, there are said to be nine minds, and the path of seeing is complete. By the power of the second, there is said to be one mind, meaning that the path of seeing is complete solely in dependence on the one mind-class corresponding to the wisdom that realises suchness. Here too there is a calm-abiding path, to be understood as before.

items.zh: 又立二分見道所斷煩惱隨眠。一、隨逐清淨色，二、隨逐心心所。由見道中止觀雙運，故聖弟子俱時能捨止觀二道所斷隨眠。第一、觀所斷，第二、止所斷。是故見道說名究竟。若言觀品所攝諸智見斷隨眠隨逐生者，應不得名對治體性。由此因緣，薄伽梵說：隨信行者、隨法行者入見道時，名為第六行無相行補特伽羅。非信勝解、見得、身證、慧脫、俱脫，五得其名。由彼於滅住寂靜想，是故說彼名住無相。

items.title: Section: The Skilled Physician Lancing a Wound

items.zh: 譬如良醫拔毒箭者，知癰熟已，利刀先剖，膿雖漸出，猶未頓盡，後更廣開周迴𮊞搦；膿出漉盡，未能甚淨，瘡門尚開，為令斂故，或以膩團、或以膩帛而帖塞之，如是漸次肌肉得斂。令義易了，故作此喻。
items.en: Just as a skilled physician extracting a poisoned arrow, knowing an abscess has matured, first lances it with a sharp blade — the pus, though it drains, does not do so all at once, and so the physician must further widen the opening and press repeatedly around it; once the pus has fully drained, the wound is still not perfectly clean, its opening still remaining, and so, to help it close, an oily compress or oiled cloth is applied, the flesh gradually contracting thereafter. This analogy is given to make the meaning easy to understand. For this reason, the Blessed One said: the faith-follower and the dharma-follower, upon entering the path of seeing, are together named the sixth kind of person practising the mark-free path. The other five, conviction-adherent, one-who-has-arrived-at-vision, body-witness, wisdom-liberated, and both-liberated, are not so named, since, already abiding in the perception of stillness regarding cessation, they are instead called those who abide in the mark-free.

items.title: Section: Reading the Physician's Analogy Point by Point

items.zh: 此中義者，如已熟癰，當知隨順見道所斷諸漏處事亦爾。如利刀剖，當知毘鉢舍那品所攝見道亦爾。如周𮊞搦，當知奢摩他品所攝見道亦爾。如膿，當知一切見道所斷隨眠漏亦爾。如瘡未淨、未斂，當知修道所斷諸漏漏事亦爾。如膩團帛，當知修道亦爾。若諸異生離欲界欲、或色界欲，但由修道，無有見道。彼於欲界得離欲時，貪欲、瞋恚及彼隨法隣近憍慢，若諸煩惱相應無明不現行故，皆說名斷。非如見道所斷薩迦耶見等。由彼諸惑住此身中，從定起已，有時現行，非生上者彼復現起。
items.en: The meaning here is this: as with the matured abscess, so too the state of affairs bound up with the outflows severed by the path of seeing. As with the sharp blade's lancing, so too the path of seeing belonging to the insight category. As with the surrounding pressing, so too the path of seeing belonging to the calm-abiding category. As with the pus, so too all the latent outflows severed by the path of seeing. As with the wound not yet clean or healed, so too the state of affairs bound up with the outflows severed by the path of cultivation. As with the oily compress, so too the path of cultivation. If ordinary beings become free of desire for the desire realm or the form realm purely through cultivation, without any path of seeing, then, upon becoming free of desire for the desire realm, their greed, hatred, and the conceit closely bound up with these, along with any affliction-associated ignorance, no longer manifest, and this too is called severing — but not like the severing of self-view and the rest at the path of seeing. Because these afflictions still dwell within that very body, they will manifest again upon emerging from absorption, though they will not manifest again in one reborn into a higher realm.

items.zh: 如是異生離色界欲，如其所應除瞋恚，餘煩惱，當知亦爾。自地所有見斷諸

blocks.text: How affliction is cured, ending with the simile of a skilled physician lancing an abscess.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the path of seeing cuts only a portion, the conceptual afflictions, and is the "partial" antidote; the path of cultivation aims at cutting all.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the four preparatory stages are close to severing, and so are the "near" antidote. (Untranslated, 0624c27: when one rises to the path of seeing, the noble wisdom takes suffering as object but does not discriminate "this is suffering"; it is freed from every mark and proliferation, and rests on suchness alone.)

Master Cháng Bǎi: counting nine or sixteen minds is a description with elaboration; inwardly realising suchness, free of names, it is one. (Untranslated, 0625a16: in the path of seeing, calm and insight are united, so latent tendencies cut by both are abandoned at once; those entering are "dwelling in the signless".)
Master Cháng Bǎi: the simile makes severing easy to understand. Having seen the truths, they dwell in the "perception" of signless cessation.

The sharp blade is the insight of seeing, which severs; the pressing is calm. The pus is what is cut at seeing; the unhealed wound, what remains for cultivation. Master Cháng Bǎi: worldly cultivation cuts only what blocks absorption; at times, on emerging, the afflictions can appear again.
The abscess is lanced at once, but the wound heals slowly. Seeing the truth is sudden; becoming free in daily life takes time.

quiz.q: What does each of the four antidotes refer to?
options: maturation: four roots; near: seeing; partial: cultivation; complete: adepts
maturation: thirteen requisites; near-severing: four roots; partial: seeing; complete: cultivation
all four are cultivation
all four are seeing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the path of seeing severs only a portion, the conceptual afflictions of the three realms, and so is the partial antidote; the path of cultivation aims at severing all and is the complete antidote. Maturation builds the capacity in one's continuum.

quiz.q: The English has "the roots of goodness belonging to heat, summit..." What is left out?
options: nothing: 決擇分 merely names this section of the treatise, the four roots belonging to the accumulation stage, as the lecture says, so that the omission is reasonable
it omits 決擇分, the defining name, near decisive discernment of reality
it omits 善根
it omits 世第一法
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these four preparatory stages are wholesome roots of faith through wisdom, within the discernment of reality; being close to severing, they are the near-severing antidote. 決擇分 explains why, and the English's omission drops the reason for the name.

quiz.q: What are the two rationales for establishing the path of seeing?
options: the hearers' and the bodhisattvas' rationales
sudden and gradual awakening
propagating the teaching, with elaboration; inwardly realising the ultimate, free of elaboration
the two truths of convention and ultimate alone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: setting up nine or sixteen minds in the names of the teaching is establishment with elaboration; inwardly realising the ultimate principle of suchness, free of names and false discrimination, is establishment free of elaboration, the true attainment. The English matches.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the nine minds and the one mind?
options: eight subsequent insights plus one pure-calm mind of root wisdom; one mind rests on suchness-wisdom
nine stages of seeing, passed in nine sittings; one mind means undistracted concentration, unrelated to suchness-wisdom, the two being successive
nine consciousnesses; the store-consciousness
nine attainments; cessation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: eight subsequent insights and one pure calm-abiding mind on which root non-conceptual wisdom rests make nine; solely by the class of mind joined with root wisdom realising suchness, there is the one-mind true path of seeing. The two describe one breakthrough.

quiz.q: §44 places "For this reason, the Blessed One said" after the physician simile. What is wrong against the lecture's text?
options: no problem: 由此因緣 refers to the simile, the order matching the lecture's source text exactly
the whole of §44 should be deleted
the order is reversed: in the source it precedes the simile, following the question on insight; placed after, 由此因緣 points wrongly
it should be moved to §1
quiz.why: In the lecture's source text, this sentence comes before the simile. Master Cháng Bǎi: to make the principle of severing affliction easy to understand, the simile of the physician is introduced. So the simile does not cause the Buddha's statement, and the placement in the Chinese and English sections misleads.

quiz.q: The English has "cessation's still, quiet state." What word has shifted?
options: nothing: 想 means state here, the attainment of cessation, all five having entered it, as the lecture says, "perception" suggesting deluded thought
滅 as "cessation" is wrong and should be "death"
想 became "state": the lecture says abiding in a quiet perception; 想 is not a state
住 as "abiding" is wrong and should be "leaving"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having seen the noble truths, they can abide in the quiet perception of signless cessation, and so are called abiding in the signless, not practising it. "State" loses 想, which is the operative word; and "mark-free" for 無相 is a reasonable rendering.

quiz.q: How is the simile matched: the blade and the pressing around?
options: blade: insight-side seeing; pressing: calm-side seeing; pus: latent outflows; compress: cultivation
blade: calm-side seeing; pressing: insight-side; pus: cultivation's
blade: ethics; pressing: giving
blade: the Buddha; pressing: the Saṅgha
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi repeats the matching: the sharp blade is the insight side of seeing, which severs; the pressing is the calm side. The pus is what is severed at seeing; the unhealed wound the outflows left for cultivation; and the compress the path of cultivation. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: Ordinary beings' worldly cultivation is called severing. Why is it unlike the severing at seeing?
options: worldly cultivation is stronger, severing seeds, so that ordinary beings never fall back, while seeing only sees truth and severs nothing
only manifestation is severed, not seeds; afflictions stay in the store-consciousness and manifest after absorption
they are exactly the same
ordinary beings sever nothing at all
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this is contaminated cultivation, severing only the manifestation that obstructs absorption, not the seeds severed at seeing; the afflictions stay in the store-consciousness and may manifest on emerging from absorption. This also explains why absorption does not guarantee non-regression.

quiz.q: The English has "they will manifest again upon emerging from absorption." What is omitted?
options: it omits 有時: at times, not necessarily; the English is too strong
nothing: they surely manifest on emerging, as the lecture stresses, 有時 being an empty word, and "will" rightly showing they certainly recur
it omits 定
it omits 起
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi says that on emerging from absorption these afflictions can still manifest. The treatise qualifies this with 有時, at times. The English "will manifest" turns a possibility into a certainty. The clause on those reborn higher, which do not manifest, is rendered correctly.
